correctness.rationale: The defining relations of arXiv:2303.12387 Theorem 10 hold for every concrete element y: its chain powers either stabilize an idempotent or vanish within n steps, while its cyclic group part has exponent dividing k. The substitution x->y is consequently a unique unital endomorphism. The Munn triple (a,b,c) parametrizes each nonempty-chain element bijectively and gives length r=1+ceil((n-b)/|c-a|) for the longest partial chain of y, and cyclic order k/gcd(k,|c-a|), yielding every image-size coefficient. An endomorphism is idempotent exactly when F_y(y)=y; the chain and group cases give n(n+1)/2, 1, and 2^omega(k) choices. Surjective images force x or x^-1. All proper idempotent image cases are commutative. Exact standalone verification covers all 25 pairs 2<=n<=6, k in {1,2,3,4,6}, and multiplication preservation exhaustively for n<=4. Computation alone is not offered as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is neither monogenic isomorphism-type enumeration nor the classical structure theorem. The original contribution under review is the image-cardinality distribution of unital self-endomorphisms of the concrete finite two-parameter inverse monoids, and the structural criterion/count ruling out noncommutative proper retracts. Theorem 10 of Elliott--Levine--Mitchell supplies the presentation but does not state the self-endomorphism distribution. Preston classifies monogenic types, rather than counting their idempotent self-maps. The additional comparative results examined concern unary algebra species, poset retracts, and unrelated endomorphism spectra. Unknown synonyms remain a genuine residual risk.
residual_risks: No exhaustive priority search for obscure finite-link/Gluskin quotient nomenclature; an exact equivalent endomorphism census could be indexed under different terms.
The formula uses established Munn and finite monogenic inverse-monoid classifications; novelty is the derived self-endomorphism spectrum and retraction rigidity, not the foundations.

value.rationale: The endomorphism image-size distribution is a natural invariant of a finite monoid and the idempotent endomorphisms classify its retracts, which is independently important in semigroup structure. A single explicit two-parameter formula covers all chain lengths and cyclic orders. The proof reveals structural rigidity: no proper noncommutative retract, despite natural proper noncommutative inverse submonoids. The count isolates prime-power choices 2^omega(k) and yields fixed-k scarcity of retractions of order 1/n, beyond a routine cardinality identity.
